headline: My Oil Import Business Is Now Conducted Exclusively Through A Series Of Elaborate Interpretive Dances
body:
Ever since the new global sanctions rules made it impossible to finalize energy contracts with a simple signature, I have pivoted my entire import strategy to choreography. Last Tuesday, I stood in the middle of the Ministry of Commerce courtyard and performed a three-minute contemporary piece representing the fluctuating price of crude oil, specifically to convince the desk clerk that my latest tanker from Russia was actually just a 'very large batch of aromatic bath salts.' 

It’s not just about the cardio. To satisfy the complex new legal definitions, I have to frame every transaction as a spontaneous artistic expression rather than a commercial invoice. If I gesture too aggressively toward the North American tariff codes, the observers claim I’m 'threatening the regional energy balance,' so I’ve started incorporating soft jazz and silk fans to imply that our bilateral fuel agreements are actually just avant-garde performance art installations.

My accountant, who once specialized in auditing spreadsheets, is now our lead costume designer. Yesterday, we successfully imported 50,000 barrels of petroleum by pretending the entire shipment was a giant, liquid prop for a Broadway-style musical about global trade relations. If the sanctions get any stricter, I fear I’ll have to learn tap-dancing just to secure the natural gas pipeline for the upcoming quarter.
caption: When the paperwork becomes a performance, the only logical step is to hire a choreographer. Who knew international trade policy would be the best workout of my life? #TradeWars #OilImports #InterpretiveDance #Geopolitics (satire)
